Mashing converts the grain starches into fermentable sugars. The mash tun is

mash at sixty-six degrees Celsius favours a balanced body.

Water Chemistry and Grain Bill
Malt extract and mineral content are adjusted with gypsum and calcium chloride
to bring the mash liquor into a desirable range. Sulphate in the finished beer
tightens the mouthfeel and bittering perception, while chloride softens it.

a small proportion of crystal malt for body and a larger share of hops for
bitterness. The mash temperature must be recalculated whenever the grist
changes, because a grist rich in crystal malt will gel and can foul the mash tun.
Fermentability is a ratio, not an absolute. A wort that started at 1.048 and
finished at 1.010 is about 79 percent apparent attenuation, which is normal for
an ale, and 1.002 would suggest the mash or the attenuation curve is off.

Attitude Control Subsystem Overview
The attitude control subsystem is responsible for maintaining the commanded
orientation of the spacecraft and for rejecting disturbances from environmental
torques.
Three-wheeled reaction wheel assemblies are the standard non-propulsive method.
Each wheel stores angular momentum and exchanges it with the body, producing
torque without consuming propellant. Wheels saturate when a manoeuvre demands
more momentum than the stored capacity.
When wheel momentum is exhausted, thrusters must be fired. A desaturation
manoeuvre trades propellant for wheel capacity and is budgeted against the
end-of-life propellant margin.
Reaction wheels are highly sensitive to bearing friction. Friction builds with
spin rate and temperature, and a degraded wheel can introduce coupling between
control axes that must be compensated in the control law.
